title: Python Sets: Union, Intersection & Difference in 1 Line
description:
Lists and dicts get all the attention, but Python sets quietly do math-class set operations with a single symbol -- no loops required. In this Short we compare two sets with |, &, and -, then show why membership checks on a set beat scanning a list every time.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/python-mastery-path/level-1/05-data-structures/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Ever needed to compare two lists for what's shared, what's unique, or what's different? Python sets can do all of that with one single symbol, and zero loops.
Start with two sets -- just curly braces around unique values.
The pipe symbol gives you the union of both sets, the ampersand gives you the intersection -- what they share -- and a minus sign gives you the difference.
And checking membership is near instant with a set -- way faster than scanning through a list.

display.code: print(3 in a)  # membership test: True

beats.narration: That's the real reason sets exist: fast, unique, math-style comparisons. Full lesson's linked below.
